Switch between millimeters and inches fo: Switch between millimeters and inches for dimensions, gaps, and rulers. A 25.4 mm part remains exactly one inch wide.
This changes how measurements appear. Im: This changes how measurements appear. Import and export units have their own controls.
The gap is the shortest space between tw: The gap is the shortest space between two cut outlines. Increase it for a wider tool, heat clearance, or easier part removal.
Set the gap to zero when neighboring par: Set the gap to zero when neighboring parts should share a laser cut. Stock edges receive the same clearance.
4 orientations allow 0°, 90°, 180°, and: 4 orientations allow 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270°. With 8, the search can also use 45° steps. Use 1 when parts must keep their orientation.
More angles help irregular shapes, but e: More angles help irregular shapes, but expand the search. Four is a useful starting point for rectangular parts.
Gravity favors a narrow layout and a usa: Gravity favors a narrow layout and a usable offcut. Bounding box reduces the enclosing rectangle. Compact reduces the enclosing convex area.
Bounding box is a good default. Try Grav: Bounding box is a good default. Try Gravity when you want to save a strip of material for the next job.
Smaller tolerance follows curves more cl: Smaller tolerance follows curves more closely and uses more vertices. Larger tolerance reduces the work needed to calculate a layout.
For example, 0.1 mm allows less deviatio: For example, 0.1 mm allows less deviation than 0.5 mm. Exported outlines use the same approximation. Reimport after changing it.
Nearly touching endpoints can be joined: Nearly touching endpoints can be joined into a closed cutting contour. The tolerance is the largest gap the importer may repair.
Start small. Increasing it can recover i: Start small. Increasing it can recover imperfect SVG or DXF files, but an excessive value may join edges that should stay apart. Ambiguous junctions are skipped.
For nesting, a convex envelope surrounds: For nesting, a convex envelope surrounds each part. Fewer corners can speed up complex jobs, at the cost of less tightly packed material.
The cut and exported outline stay intact: The cut and exported outline stay intact. Repeated shapes are faster when imported once and assigned a quantity.
Each worker evaluates a different candid: Each worker evaluates a different candidate. More workers can finish a generation sooner, while using more CPU and memory.
Try 2 on a laptop or 4 on a desktop. The: Try 2 on a laptop or 4 on a desktop. The interface remains responsive and Stop cancels all workers.
A unitless SVG needs a conversion from d: A unitless SVG needs a conversion from drawing units to inches. At 96 units/inch, a 96-unit square measures 25.4 mm.
Explicit physical dimensions and viewBox: Explicit physical dimensions and viewBox take priority. Choose 72, 90, 96, or your own value to match the source file.
Auto uses the DXF unit declaration. Sele: Auto uses the DXF unit declaration. Select an override when a file is unitless or was saved with the wrong unit metadata.
A one-unit line is 25.4 mm with Inches s: A one-unit line is 25.4 mm with Inches selected, or 1 mm with Millimeters. Auto treats unitless files as mm and reports that assumption.
The layout keeps its physical size while: The layout keeps its physical size while coordinates convert to the chosen unit. Inches, mm, and cm also write the matching DXF unit declaration.
Points and picas use unitless DXF coordi: Points and picas use unitless DXF coordinates because DXF has no code for those units. Use the matching import override if you bring that file back.
When two parts touch, their common edge: When two parts touch, their common edge is exported once. Partial overlaps are combined too, reducing duplicate cuts and repeated heating.
Requires zero part gap. SVG and DXF both: Requires zero part gap. SVG and DXF both support shared cuts. Use separate outlines when your downstream software expects closed individual parts.
At 0, placement focuses on material usag: At 0, placement focuses on material usage. Increasing the weight gives candidate positions with longer shared edges a better score.
Use exact outlines, shared lines, and ze: Use exact outlines, shared lines, and zero gap. Rough approximation skips contact scoring. This is a preference, not a machine-time estimate; try 0.5 first.
Each generation contains several differe: Each generation contains several different part orders and rotations. The best candidate survives; successful candidates combine to produce the next generation.
A small population moves quickly. A larg: A small population moves quickly. A larger one explores more alternatives. Start at 10, then increase it for a difficult layout.
Mutation changes neighboring part order: Mutation changes neighboring part order and allowed rotations. A higher percentage introduces more variation into each generation.
Try 10% first. Increase it when the sear: Try 10% first. Increase it when the search repeats similar arrangements; lower it to spend more effort refining successful ones.
Search until stopped keeps producing gen: Search until stopped keeps producing generations. A fixed evaluation budget limits the number of candidate layouts to try.
Use a budget larger than the population: Use a budget larger than the population to explore several generations. Stop always keeps the best completed layout, ready to export.
